title: Fenced local-first render lifecycle
description:
As a render customer, I want one authoritative attempt owner so that stale workers cannot publish output or double-charge me.

Feature: Fenced local-first rendering
Scenario: Competing local claim and cloud reservation
 Given an eligible queued job at its original grace deadline
 When a local claim and cloud reservation race
 Then only one conditional transaction succeeds and the loser cannot own the job
Scenario: Stale completion
 Given an expired or superseded generation
 When its worker publishes completion
 Then no authoritative artifact or settlement changes
Scenario: Cancellation ordering
 Given an active render
 When cancellation commits before completion
 Then old tokens cannot complete and uncertain remote work retains its slot
Scenario: Completed job cancellation
 Given completion already committed
 When cancellation arrives
 Then the job remains succeeded
Scenario: Bounded leases and retries
 Given authoritative server time and two total attempts or one cloud attempt
 When heartbeats or failures occur
 Then no lease exceeds the absolute deadline and exhausted attempts never requeue
Scenario: Unknown cloud submission
 Given a reserved attempt with uncertain paid submission
 When failure or cancellation is finalized
 Then operator reservation and slot remain held until required proof while customer refund is exactly once

Canonical VideoML initiative D09/D09a/D09b is binding for every edge, prohibited edge, field and transaction predicate. P18 defines pure decisions and persistence contract; cloud execution and deployed cutover are later packets.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Superseded by the combined Auritus and Babulus plan (epic babulus-d22d6854). Video jobs reuse the Auritus claim and fallback design, extended in M3 and M4 with a real claim renewal, a fencing token and the spending checks, so the separate fenced render lifecycle is dropped.
